To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inbound tour operators (ITOs) in our sample, who were responsible for the purchase of tourism products on the behalf of their clients, considered price, product quality and service as the most important supplier attributes in their purchase decision.

the ITOs in the sample are: (i) more concerned about price than quality when purchasing hotels, coach companies or restaurants, (ii) more concerned about quality than price for coach companies and restaurants, and (iii) more concerned about product quality than product price when purchasing hotels.

Japanese inbound tour operators place more importance on the following supplier attributes than Asian inbound tour operators do: - the ability to offer unique products, - the ability to provide a wide range of services, - the ability of the salesperson to understand their business and the needs of their clients, - the ability and willingness of the supplier to offer a range of products to meet the needs of the ITOs clients.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) The importance of supplier attributes in the purchase of three types of tourism product: hotels, coach and restaurants; (2) Differences between the attitudes of inbound tour operators in their purchase of tourism products for the Japanese and Asian markets; (3) The importance of the relationship between inbound tour operators and tourism suppliers

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inbound tour operator's decision making behavior is influenced by the product type, the market segment and the market served by the inbound tour operator.

the findings of this study suggest that inbound tour operators in the Asian and Japanese markets are not homogeneous in their purchasing behavior and that they differ in their attitudes toward the attributes of suppliers.
the results indicate that the ITOs in this study are not only influenced by product attributes but also by other factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inbound tour operators in the Japanese and Asian markets are similar in many respects, yet different in their purchase decision-making behavior and buyer attitudes.

the inbound tour operators in Australia are a critical component in the tourism channel and the decision making process of the ITO is complex, with the purchase decision influenced by a number of factors.

there is no single set of supplier attributes which are of importance to ITOs, rather the importance of these attributes varies depending on the product type, the market segment and the market segment of the tour operator.
The main takeaway from our work is that

inbound tour operators have different attitudes toward the three types of tourism product, and that these product differences have a significant impact on the way that ITOs make their purchasing decisions.
ITOs in Australia have a strong preference for local suppliers and that they are willing to accept a lower level of quality in order to support the local industry.
inbound tour operators are a critical component in international tourism channels.
